statement: For A (n×n, invertible), C (k×k, invertible), U (n×k), V (k×n), provided C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U is invertible: (A+UCV)^{-1} = A^{-1} - A^{-1}U(C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U)^{-1}VA^{-1}.

symbols.meaning: small matrix carrying the rank-k correction
left factor of the low-rank update
right factor of the low-rank update
capacitance matrix (k x k inverse to be computed instead of the full n x n inverse)

steps.text: Derive the auxiliary identity (I+P)^{-1} = I - (I+P)^{-1}P from the trivial factorization I = (I+P)^{-1}(I+P) = (I+P)^{-1} + (I+P)^{-1}P, and symmetrically (I+P)^{-1} = I - P(I+P)^{-1}.
Derive the push-through identity (I+UV)^{-1}U = U(I+VU)^{-1} by starting from U(I+VU) = (I+UV)U and left-multiplying by (I+UV)^{-1}, right-multiplying by (I+VU)^{-1}.

Set P = UV in step 1 to get (I+UV)^{-1} = I - UV(I+UV)^{-1}. Since UV(I+UV)^{-1} = (I+UV)^{-1}UV (a matrix commutes with its own inverse-shifted product) and (I+UV)^{-1}UV = [(I+UV)^{-1}U]V, apply the push-through identity from step 2 to replace the bracket, giving the reduced Woodbury identity (I+UV)^{-1} = I - U(I+VU)^{-1}V.

Recover the general identity by substituting U ↦ A^{-1}U and V ↦ CV into the reduced identity: (I+A^{-1}UCV)^{-1} = I - A^{-1}U(I+CVA^{-1}U)^{-1}CV. Rewrite the left side as (A+UCV)^{-1}A, since A^{-1}(A+UCV) = I+A^{-1}UCV.
Right-multiply both sides by A^{-1}: (A+UCV)^{-1} = A^{-1} - A^{-1}U(I+CVA^{-1}U)^{-1}CVA^{-1}.

Fold C into the bracketed inverse: (I+CVA^{-1}U)^{-1}C = [C^{-1}(I+CVA^{-1}U)]^{-1} = (C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U)^{-1}, using (XY)^{-1}=Y^{-1}X^{-1} with X=C^{-1}, Y=(I+CVA^{-1}U). Substituting this gives the Woodbury/matrix-inversion-lemma formula: (A+UCV)^{-1} = A^{-1} - A^{-1}U(C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U)^{-1}VA^{-1}.

Verify directly: multiplying (A+UCV) by the right-hand side and collecting terms, (A+UCV)[A^{-1}-A^{-1}U(C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U)^{-1}VA^{-1}] reduces to I + UCVA^{-1} - UC(C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U)(C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U)^{-1}VA^{-1} = I + UCVA^{-1} - UCVA^{-1} = I, confirming the claimed inverse.

assumptions.breaks_when: A is singular; A^{-1} does not exist so the right-hand side is undefined.
C is singular; a separate variation of the identity (I+BVA^{-1}U in place of C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U) is required instead, per the source's 'variation for when B is singular' case.

assumptions.assumption: The capacitance matrix C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U (k×k) is invertible.
assumptions.breaks_when: C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U is singular, e.g. when the rank-k update makes A+UCV itself singular in a way that collapses this small matrix.

failure_modes.signature: C^{-1}+VA^{-1}U is singular, so its inverse cannot be formed
failure_modes.cause: the low-rank update interacts with A^{-1} such that the k×k capacitance matrix loses rank

failure_modes.signature: computed (A+UCV)^{-1} via the formula disagrees substantially with direct inversion even though A and A+UCV are both well-conditioned
failure_modes.cause: per the source, direct application of the Sherman–Morrison–Woodbury formula can be numerically unstable in finite precision even under favorable conditioning; this is an empirically reported phenomenon, not resolved by the algebra itself
